name: TX-26
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 district fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent party
Gill holds a roughly 75-to-1 cash advantage ($1.96M vs $2,500)

model.rationale: The R+11 district, Gill's overwhelming financial edge over a barely funded challenger, and market pricing near certainty all point to a comfortable Republican hold; with no public polling available, uncertainty stays elevated but nowhere near enough to put the outcome in doubt.
model.watch: A surprise poll showing a single-digit race or significant outside spending against Gill would be the main signal of a genuine shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 26th District, drawn with an R+11 partisan lean, makes first-term Republican Brandon Gill the heavy favorite over Democrat Steven Shook, with Libertarian Phil Gray also on the ballot. Gill has raised $7.3 million and holds nearly $2 million on hand, while Shook has raised about $32,000 and reported just $2,500 in the bank, leaving the Democrat little capacity to reach voters. Prediction markets price Gill's reelection around 97%.

No public general-election polls are available and no expert raters have listed the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. A Democratic wave would need to be historically large to erase a double-digit structural deficit in this seat. The realistic question is the size of Gill's winning margin rather than who wins.
